cards.lore: 100 years of debt slavery disguised as economic stability. Cut out these cards, play the game, and watch the illusion burn.
cards.name: Uncle FrizzleBob's Federal Reserve Secret
cards.power: Pattern Recognition: If opponents read the fine print on their money, draw 2 cards.

cards.lore: It’s not Federal, and there is no Reserve. A private banking cartel that bought the right to print your money.
cards.name: The Creature from the Fed
cards.power: Spawn: Take 1 labor token from every player turn. You are the Creature.

cards.lore: Olde Money is printed. If typed into existence is real, backed by the promises your grandparents will pay it back.
cards.name: Fiat Conjuring
cards.power: Generate 10 debt tokens from nothing. Laugh. Carry inflation.

cards.lore: Of all the sciences, the science of monetary complexity is chosen the fraud… — John Kenneth Galbraith
cards.name: Economic Jargon
cards.power: Paralyze one opponent with confusion. They lose a turn (asking monetary policy).

cards.lore: The blueprint. King William III needed war debts. Bankers gave him 1.2M out of nowhere and created a private bank wearing a state mask.
cards.name: Bank of England (1694)
cards.power: Loan your opponent 5 tokens. Demand 10 tokens back.

cards.lore: Goldsmith realized only 5% of people ask for gold at once. They learned all the power was belief.
cards.name: Fractional Reserve Illusion
cards.power: Roll 10 dice when you have 1. Fool’s Gold is real.

cards.lore: The missing founding. First private U.S. bank before the Constitution. War needed funding before freedom.
cards.name: Bank of North America (1781)
cards.power: I print war. Every dollar you use funds my next one.

cards.lore: If debt exists, let the elite own it. Hamilton wanted a central bank; history politely agreed.
cards.name: Alexander Hamilton's Ghost
cards.power: Federalize your fate. A National Banker. Power beats messy states.

cards.lore: Hamilton’s pet project. Loaned the government 8.2M, gained prices by 1792, and made the bankers rich.
cards.name: First Bank of the U.S.
cards.power: Siphon 20% of wealth, then sell the same stock to private investors.

cards.lore: I believe that banking institutions are more dangerous to our liberties than standing armies.
cards.name: Thomas Jefferson's Warning
cards.power: Read an opponent’s hidden cards. Shock: You are right.

cards.lore: Born in the War of 1812. Another monopoly over money and speculation that hurt the working class.
cards.name: Second Bank of the U.S.
cards.power: Take the gold. Cause inflation. Blame someone else.

cards.lore: I killed the bank and all I got was this weird election and a duel. 1832: the only time in history.
cards.name: Andrew Jackson Kills a Bank
cards.power: Cancel one monopoly effect. Lose 2 health for dramatic effect.

cards.lore: Railroads, Carnegie, Vanderbilts, Rockefeller. Competition was cute. Scale, oil, rails. Next stop: governing money itself.
cards.name: The Gilded Oligarchs
cards.power: Monopolize 1 resource. Opponents pay 2 and do nothing.

cards.lore: He wasn't just playing the market; he was the market. Street runs out of cash, banker king of the Panic becomes king of the rescue.
cards.name: Pierpont Morgan (The Panic Maker)
cards.power: Start a rumor. Target banks lose their hand.

cards.lore: When confidence breaks, the panic does the rest. The public begged for a solution. The bankers provided one.
cards.name: The Panic of 1907
cards.power: Trigger a bank run. All players pay 5 tokens to your hand.

cards.lore: Private meeting on Jekyll Island. Write the banking cartel (1911). The public has to believe this was their idea.
cards.name: The Aldrich Plan
cards.power: Propose a new law. If rejected, redraw it in private.

cards.lore: Secret meeting of America’s richest men with fake names. What if private bankers wrote public banking law?
cards.name: Jekyll Island Duck Hunt
cards.power: Arrange the next 3 deck cards to your advantage. Lie about it.

cards.lore: Rockefeller’s father-in-law. The legislative inside man on the train of old money.
cards.name: Nelson Aldrich (The Fixer)
cards.power: Bribe a politician. Change one rule instantly.

cards.lore: Respectfully old, European and wise. If I know central banking and you don’t, trust me, I’m saving you.
cards.name: Paul Warburg (The Architect)
cards.power: Rewrite game rules. Call it Reform. Opponents must agree.

cards.lore: I was as secretive, indeed as furtive as any conspirator. Jekyll Island happened.
cards.name: Frank Vanderlip's Confession
cards.power: Confess to a crime. If nobody notices, draw 2 cards.

cards.lore: Federal Reserve Act: Publicly sold as decentralization. Privately a private banking cartel wrapped in patriotic wrapping paper.
cards.name: The Trojan Horse Act
cards.power: Disguise a penalty as a gift. Drain an opponent’s points quietly.

cards.lore: I am a most unhappy man. I have unwittingly ruined my country by a system of credit.
cards.name: Woodrow Wilson's Pen
cards.power: Sign away your nation's rights for emergency economic need.

cards.lore: Federal Reserve passed while Congress was home for Christmas. Timing is the ultimate midnight legislative superpower.
cards.name: The Christmas Eve Smuggling
cards.power: Roll until opponents go to bed. Then pass the law.

cards.lore: Bankers designing their regulator: they don't fear audit when you own and called it federal agency.
cards.name: The Fox in the Henhouse
cards.power: Become the regulator. Ignore all penalties.

cards.lore: Over 90% of money isn’t printed. It’s typed into existence as a loan by commercial banks. They monetize your debt.
cards.name: Grigsged (Book Money)
cards.power: Create 50 tokens from nothing. Loan them out. Demand 10x back.

cards.lore: When money is created as debt, the principal is created but the interest is not. The system demands infinite growth and guaranteed bankruptcies.
cards.name: The Interest Trap
cards.power: Create money for the principal, but not interest. Watch players fight.

cards.lore: Price stability? Consumer prices are 30x higher today than in 1913. Inflation is a hidden tax created by expanding the money supply.
cards.name: Purchasing Power Theft
cards.power: Do nothing. All opponents’ tokens lose 10% value per turn.

cards.lore: Federal Reserve notes are backed by the future taxation of Americans. When bankers gamble and lose, the taxpayer is the collateral.
cards.name: The Taxpayer Backstop
cards.power: When you lose a bet, force the poorest player to pay.

cards.lore: The Fed pumped the money supply, fueling a drunken decade and the cheap credit that made the biggest speculative bubble in U.S. history.
cards.name: The Roaring 20s Bubble
cards.power: Inflate everyone. Draw 2 cards. Next turn everyone discards their hand.

cards.lore: The bubble popped. Instead of liquidity, the Fed contracted the money supply, turning a crash into a decade of mass poverty.
cards.name: The Great Depression
cards.power: Contract the money supply. Skip everyone’s turn. Starve the board.

cards.lore: Economists admitted the truth. The Fed created the panic, directly caused and exacerbated the greatest economic disaster.
cards.name: Milton Friedman's Diagnosis
cards.power: Blame your wise ugly professor after everyone is dead.

cards.lore: At Friedman’s 90th birthday: Regarding the Great Depression. You’re right, we did it. We’re very sorry. But thanks to you, we won’t do it again.
cards.name: Bernanke's Hollow Apology
cards.power: Say “I’m sorry.” Become immune to consequences.

cards.lore: In 1934, the government seized the people’s gold. The ultimate theft: physical wealth swapped for a paper substitute.
cards.name: The 1934 Gold Heist
cards.power: Confiscate hard assets. Replace wealth with paper.

cards.lore: Once the Fed held your real gold. They issued Gold Certificates—bookkeeping ghosts from the Treasury representing assets they don’t possess.
cards.name: Gold Certificates
cards.power: Show a shiny note using trust instead of points.

cards.lore: The Federal Reserve possesses no gold at all. We know this under gold since 1934. The General Counsel admits the emperor is naked.
cards.name: Scott Alvarez's Denial
cards.power: Speak legal gibberish until the audience gives up.

cards.lore: The Fed’s balance sheet values its phantom gold at statutory price of $42.22 an ounce, ignoring reality for bookkeeping sorcery.
cards.name: The $422 Arbitrary Peg
cards.power: Declare a single token worth 50 because a law says so.

cards.lore: Public face. Appointed by the President, but they answer to no one, cannot be fired, and laugh at Congressional funding.
cards.name: Board of Governors
cards.power: Appoint friends to a fake oversight board. Gain 2 Influence.

cards.lore: The 12 regional banks are 100% privately owned by member banks. Public central bank, private dividend machine.
cards.name: The Regional Reserve Banks
cards.power: Force opponents to buy monopoly shares. Pay yourself guaranteed dividends.

cards.lore: Representing the massive Wall Street banks, the NY Fed exerts final dominance, operating with zero public accountability.
cards.name: The New York Fed
cards.power: Live infinitely. You are the only player who matters.

cards.lore: Private bankers and corporate interests sit on the committee that sets the nation’s interest rates, steering the economy for their portfolios.
cards.name: The F.O.M.C. (Open Market Committee)
cards.power: Secretly change card costs. Watch everyone panic.

cards.lore: The perfect predatory loan, bundled for trade, sold. When the casino collapsed, they learned the public never leaves the table.
cards.name: The 2008 Subprime Crash
cards.power: Gamble everything. Lose twice: first in bad debt, then in public trust.

cards.lore: QE is trillion-dollar money creation pushed straight to the top of the pyramid while everyone else gets inflation.
cards.name: Quantitative Easing
cards.power: Print infinite tokens. Hand to banks. Call it stabilization.

cards.lore: Government bails out banks. Government issues debt. Banks buy those bonds with bailout money and charge the taxpayer interest.
cards.name: The Ouroboros Rescue
cards.power: Borrow to buy out control so that the guy you borrowed from lives.

cards.lore: Lose? Please. I’m too systemically important. If I fall, the whole economy gets blamed.
cards.name: Too Big to Fail (T.B.T.F.)
cards.power: Threaten to destroy the board if you lose.

cards.lore: Founded 1921 by Morgan allies. A factory placing bankers, CIA directors, and politicians into a single globalist hive-mind.
cards.name: Council on Foreign Relations
cards.power: Take over an opponent’s turn. Claim it was foreign policy.

cards.lore: The central bank of central banks in Basel. Private, sovereign entity above the law, coordinating global feudalism in secret.
cards.name: Bank for Int. Settlements (B.I.S.)
cards.power: You are immune to all laws. Period.

cards.lore: A worldwide system of financial control, able to dominate the political system of each country. — Carroll Quigley. Absolute control.
cards.name: The Feudal Endgame (N.W.O.)
cards.power: Consolidate power. Game over. You own everything.

cards.lore: They say the crashes they engineer are the explicit justification to expand from G7 to G20, centralizing planetary economic power.
cards.name: Global Governance (G20)
cards.power: Use a crisis you created to demand global authority.

cards.lore: Ron Paul’s grassroots movement terrified the cartel. The Fed fought sunlight like vampires fight mirrors.
cards.name: The Audit Movement
cards.power: Look at any player’s hidden hand. Expose cheating. Force public receipts.

cards.lore: From Boston to Wall Street, people got wise to money magic. Once peasants learn accounting, every empire sweats.
cards.name: End the Fed Protests
cards.power: Form a coalition. Combine points to overthrow the leader.

cards.lore: A state-owned bank that actually works. It partners local banks, keeps capital in the community, and outperforms the Wall Street casino regularly.
cards.name: Bank of North Dakota
cards.power: Keep money local. Ignore macroeconomic penalties.

cards.lore: Public banks redirect deposits at the Fed into 2–3% government interest. Public banking cuts parasites, not funding. Mrs. Street smiles.
cards.name: Ellen Brown (Public Banking)
cards.power: Move tokens out of capital pit into protected local trash.

cards.lore: A local currency backed by human labor. Your +$10 note trades actual people with actual neighbors for actual potatoes.
cards.name: Ithaca Hours
cards.power: Trade skills. Bypass the bank’s toll entirely.

cards.lore: Armed with graphic design and arrogance, he created millions in mutual credit economic activity. A decentralized money revolution.
cards.name: The Time-Barter Rogue
cards.power: Draw your own card. It is now legally binding.

cards.lore: A completely decentralized network. No central server, no CEO, hard-capped supply of 21 million. Mathematics > manipulation.
cards.name: Bitcoin (The Protocol)
cards.power: Opt out. Start a new game where no one can print cards.

cards.lore: If you trust money to stay power, you trust it to your enemy. If the motion inflation is, it is your own strategy to solve money.
cards.name: The Un-Printable Math
cards.power: Lock assets. They cannot be inflated or diluted.

cards.lore: Once the Federal Reserve has fully unraveled for 100 years, the system collapses under disbelief. The illusion requires your belief.
cards.name: The Paradigm Shift
cards.power: Reveal truth. Throw the rigged rulebook in the trash.

cards.lore: Local action beats politics. Build alternative networks, use sound money, and quietly starve the beast of its hollow compliance.
cards.name: The Counter-Economy (Agorism)
cards.power: Play off-board. Conduct secret, untaxable trades.

cards.lore: The next century is a choice: a continuation of feudal debt slavery, or a world of trade, decentralization, and human empowerment.
cards.name: The Century of Empowerment
cards.power: Win the game by realizing you don’t need the bank to play.

cards.lore: The final move has always been to hand this myth to people: step into this epistemic sabotage as you stay fluffy. And burn the ledger.
cards.name: Kayfabizarro Anarchy
cards.power: Print cards. Leave in coffee shops. Break the spell.
